question: Under California law, may a PWC be legally operated if its lanyard-type engine cut-off switch or throttle has been altered so it no longer works as intended?
choice_a: Yes, as long as the operator still wears a PFD
choice_b: No -- it is illegal to operate a PWC if the engine cut-off switch or throttle has been altered in a way that would impede or prevent the switch from operating as intended
choice_c: Yes, altering the cut-off switch is allowed if done by a licensed marine mechanic
choice_d: Yes, but only on PWCs built before December 4, 2019
explanation: California Harbors and Navigation Code Section 655.7(b) prohibits operating a personal watercraft if its engine cut-off switch or throttle has been altered in a way that would impede or prevent the switch from working as intended.

question: Under California's PWC 'reasonable and prudent manner' operating standard, which specific maneuver near another vessel is expressly identified as reckless operation?
choice_a: Following at any distance behind a larger vessel
choice_b: Operating parallel to another vessel at a constant distance
choice_c: Jumping or attempting to jump the wake of another vessel within 100 feet
choice_d: Passing another vessel on its port side at slow-no-wake speed
explanation: Harbors and Navigation Code Section 655.7(c) specifically names jumping or attempting to jump the wake of another vessel within 100 feet as an example of reckless PWC operation.

question: Which of the following is specifically named in California law as reckless operation of a personal watercraft?
choice_a: Maintaining a slow, steady speed while passing through a swimming area at idle
choice_b: Idling the engine while anchored offshore
choice_c: Operating in a straight line away from other vessels at reduced speed
choice_d: Operating the PWC toward a person or vessel in the water and turning sharply at close range so as to spray them
explanation: Section 655.7(c) names operating toward a person or vessel in the water and turning sharply at close range so as to spray the vessel or person as an example of reckless PWC operation.

question: California law defines reckless PWC operation to include operating at what kind of speed and proximity relative to another vessel?
choice_a: A speed and proximity to another vessel such that either operator is required to swerve at the last minute to avoid a collision
choice_b: Any speed above idle within a marked no-wake zone
choice_c: Any speed that exceeds the posted speed limit by more than 5 mph
choice_d: Operating alongside another vessel while matching its speed and heading
explanation: Section 655.7(c) defines reckless operation to include operating at a rate of speed and proximity to another vessel such that either operator is required to swerve at the last minute to avoid a collision.

question: What overall operating standard does California law require of every personal watercraft 'at all times'?
choice_a: The PWC must be operated at the vessel's maximum rated speed
choice_b: The PWC must be operated in a reasonable and prudent manner
choice_c: The PWC must remain within 50 feet of the shoreline at all times
choice_d: The PWC must be operated only by its registered owner
explanation: Harbors and Navigation Code Section 655.7(c) requires that every personal watercraft be operated in a reasonable and prudent manner at all times, then gives specific examples of conduct that violates that standard.

question: Who is exempt from California's sunset-to-sunrise ban on operating a personal watercraft?
choice_a: Any PWC displaying a working headlight
choice_b: Rental PWCs operated under the supervision of a licensed guide
choice_c: Marine patrol, harbor police, or emergency personnel performing their duties
choice_d: No one is exempt under any circumstance
explanation: Harbors and Navigation Code Section 655.7(d) exempts marine patrol, harbor police, or emergency personnel performing their duties from the sunset-to-sunrise ban on PWC operation.

question: If a PWC is towing a person on water skis, how old must the required observer (in addition to the operator) be under California law?
choice_b: There is no minimum age for the observer
explanation: Harbors and Navigation Code Section 658(a) requires a person at least 12 years old, in addition to the operator, to be aboard in a position to observe anyone being towed on water skis.
